sections.h2: What are the options for selling quickly in North Brunswick?
sections.html:
An owner here can hire an agent, go it alone, or accept an as-is purchase, and the township's paperwork applies in each case. North Brunswick spans 12.03 square miles of land in Middlesex County. QuickFacts lists 45,097 residents for July 2025, up 2.8% since the 2020 base, with owners living in 57.1% of homes, far above neighboring New Brunswick.

A median owner-occupied value of $431,500 and a median household income of $120,764 describe the 2020 to 2024 picture. A buyer who needs a mortgage depends on an appraisal and a lender-approved closing date. If you cannot wait for that sequence, an as-is purchase removes the lender from the timeline.

  • Compare the net from each route after fees, repairs and carrying costs.
  • Ask the township what inspection or certificate must come before closing.
  • Request a payoff statement so the mortgage can be cancelled of record.

The township touches East Brunswick, Milltown, New Brunswick and South Brunswick in Middlesex County, plus Franklin Township in Somerset County. The Lenape lived here first, and European settlers bought the land in 1772. A state act made it a township on February 21, 1798, and later splits created East Brunswick in 1860 and Milltown in 1889.

Lawrence Brook drains the area, and its watershed covers 48 square miles across five towns. Farrington Lake, a freshwater reservoir, sits along the boundary with East Brunswick and South Brunswick. Local place names include Adams, Berdines Corner, Black Horse, Franklin Park, Livingston Park, Maple Meade, Patricks Corner and Red Lion.

The northern end near New Brunswick is mostly middle class, while the southern and eastern sections tend to be more affluent. The township bought the 104.91-acre Otken Farm on Route 130 and opened it as North Brunswick Community Park in April 2007.

sections.h2: How is North Brunswick governed, and who handles a home sale?
sections.html:
The township uses the Faulkner Act's Mayor-Council-Administrator plan, one of only three municipalities in the state's 564 that do. Voters pick a mayor for four years and six council members at large for staggered three-year terms. The council approves the budget behind the municipal piece of your tax bill.

The practical contact for a seller is the Community Development department, which handles building and zoning matters. Ask it whether a Certificate of Continued Occupancy or another inspection is required before a sale, and what it takes to close out open permits. Unfinished permits for a deck, finished basement or addition can hold up a closing.

If your house contains a rented unit, ask the township clerk whether any local rent rules apply and what a buyer needs to see about the tenancy.

sections.h2: What do schools and commuting look like in North Brunswick?
sections.html:
North Brunswick Township Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through grade 12. In 2024-25 the district had eight schools and 5,926 students, a ratio of 10.2 students per teacher. Eighth graders from anywhere in Middlesex County can apply to the county magnet schools, which charge no tuition.

Drivers rely on U.S. 1, U.S. 130 and Routes 26, 27, 91 and 171, and reach the Turnpike at exits in East Brunswick and South Brunswick. Trains to Penn Station leave from the Jersey Avenue stop in New Brunswick. NJ Transit buses 811 and 814 and county shuttles serve the township, and the average trip to work takes 29.2 minutes.

sections.h2: Which community features help a North Brunswick listing?
sections.html:
Buyers look for parks, schools and shopping along the highways. Annual events include Carnevale Italiano, put on by the Italian-American Social Club, and a Heritage Day in North Brunswick Community Park that celebrates the cultures living in town. QuickFacts shows 35.9% of residents were born abroad and 50.6% speak another language at home, so a translated listing can widen your buyer pool.

Higher education is nearby as well. Part of Rutgers' School of Environmental and Biological Sciences, formerly Cook College, sits on College Farm Road off Route 1, and Chamberlain University has its New Jersey location in the township. Among adults over 25, 44.7% hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

A new NJ Transit station on the former Johnson & Johnson site on Route 1 has been proposed for years. Do not promise buyers that it will be built; describe the rail access that exists today at Jersey Avenue.

sections.h2: Which state fees and forms apply to a North Brunswick sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state's realty transfer fee when the deed is filed. At the township's median value, the higher schedule for prices over $350,000 applies, and it reaches $4.80 for each $500 of price between $200,000 and $550,000. A reduced scale exists for senior citizens, blind or disabled persons and low and moderate income housing.

Deeds between spouses, or from parent to child, are exempt from the fee. Estates need a residency form: an estate that sells property completes the GIT/REP form under its own residency status, signed by the executor or administrator. A corporation, partnership or multi-member LLC completes the GIT/REP-3 and checks box 5.

The seller residency forms rest on N.J.S.A. 54A:8-9. For nonresidents the calculation applies 10.75% to the gain, with a floor of 2% of the price in the deed.

sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded for a North Brunswick property?
sections.html:
Deeds for township properties go to the Middlesex County Clerk in New Brunswick. The clerk wants the tax block, lot and price on the deed, an original signature with the name printed beneath, and a return address. A mortgage cancellation needs the original recorded mortgage with a proper endorsement, so ask your lender for it when you request the payoff.

A deed that must be re-recorded has to state the reason and come with a new affidavit, a new seller's residency form and a new cover sheet. Owners may also subscribe to the clerk's free email alerts, which announce any document recorded against their block and lot. If you suspect fraud, call the clerk at 732-745-3364 or 732-745-3365.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell in North Brunswick?
faqs.a: Ask the township's Community Development department. It handles building and occupancy certificates, and staff can say whether a Certificate of Continued Occupancy or another inspection applies to your sale and how long it takes.

faqs.q: What is a typical home worth in North Brunswick?
faqs.a: QuickFacts reports a median owner-occupied value of $431,500 for 2020 to 2024. Actual prices depend on the section, condition and lot, so treat the median as a rough guide.

faqs.q: Where does the deed get filed?
faqs.a: With the Middlesex County Clerk's registry in the County Administration Building at 75 Bayard Street, New Brunswick. Title companies often file electronically through the county's e-recording portal.

faqs.q: Is the transfer fee due if I deed the house to my child?
faqs.a: No, a deed between parent and child is exempt from the realty transfer fee. You still file the seller residency form, because the GIT/REP-3 has no special assurance for family transfers.

faqs.q: What changes if I live in another state?
faqs.a: You complete a GIT/REP form and, unless an assurance on the GIT/REP-3 applies, prepay at least 2% of the deed price toward New Jersey income tax. A refund is possible later if your actual tax is lower.
